title: Short circuits
body: When current has two paths, it splits between them. More of it takes the easier path, the one with less resistance. It's like water at a fork in a pipe: most of it rushes down the wider side. A bare wire has almost no resistance at all.
Put a wire across a bulb and nearly all the current takes the wire. That bulb goes dark. The whole loop now has less resistance. So more current flows, and the other bulb gets brighter.
Put a wire straight across a battery and there's almost no resistance anywhere. A huge current flows, and the wire and battery heat up fast. That's a short circuit.
realWorld: Your home has fuses or circuit breakers. They cut the power when a short circuit sends too much current through the wires.
sources: OpenStax College Physics 2e, §20.6 Electric Hazards and the Human Body. https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/20-6-electric-hazards-and-the-human-body
